exposure: Sleep disorder symptoms (snoring, breathing pauses, leg twitching/jerking)
cohort: Pregnant women in their third trimester (310 Māori and 629 non-Māori)
finding: Poor sleep quality, breathing pauses during sleep, and snoring in late pregnancy were independently associated with a higher likelihood of emergency cesarean section.
mod_finding: Women who reported poor sleep quality in later pregnancy had almost twice the odds of delivering via emergency cesarean section compared to women with good sleep quality.
